title: Asynchronous Programming
content: Asynchronous programming allows programs to work on multiple tasks concurrently without blocking. In Rust, async/await syntax provides a way to write asynchronous code that looks and behaves like synchronous code. The Future trait represents a value that may not be available yet.

title: Pattern Matching
content: Pattern matching is a powerful control flow construct in Rust that allows you to compare a value against a series of patterns and execute code based on which pattern matches. The match expression must be exhaustive, meaning all possible cases must be handled.

title: Zero-Cost Abstractions
content: Zero-cost abstractions mean that the abstractions you use in Rust have no runtime overhead. The compiler optimizes your code so that high-level constructs compile down to the same machine code as if you wrote low-level code manually. This is one of Rust's key design principles.
